samples.summary: setTheme() now unconditionally re-renders the preview, which destroys DOM-only preview state (manually expanded <details>, preview scroll position) for consumers outside the diff
samples.evidence: `setTheme` at packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:443 now calls `renderPreview()` whenever the preview is visible, and `NotePreview.render()` replaces the whole subtree via `this.el.innerHTML = md.render(...)` (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:198). Two out-of-diff consumers depend on that subtree surviving between document edits: (a) the disclosure plugin emits `<details>` whose `open` attribute is source-driven only (packages/notes/src/view/details-plugin.ts:60), so a section the reader expanded by hand collapses; (b) the proportional editor↔preview scroll sync registered at packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:426-428 reads `preview.el.scrollTop` — the innerHTML replacement can clamp/reset the preview scroll and the resulting `scroll` event drives `onPreviewScroll`, pulling the CodeMirror scroller with it. In `view`/read-only mode (a shared note link, packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:112 calls setTheme on every light/dark toggle) there are no keystrokes, so this is the only thing that ever discards that state.

samples.summary: editor.dispose() does not cancel an in-flight mermaid pass; mermaid.ts keeps process-global state (passChain / loaded / initializedTheme / renderCache) that a disposed editor's pass continues to occupy
samples.evidence: `dispose()` (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:481-487) tears down scroll/pointer listeners and destroys the CodeMirror view, but there is no hook to stop `renderMermaidBlocks`. A pass started by the last `render()` before unmount still awaits `import('mermaid')`, still runs `mermaid.initialize()`/`mermaid.render()`, still appends and removes its `d<id>` host div on `document.body`, and — because `passChain` in packages/notes/src/view/mermaid.ts is a single module-global promise chain shared by every NotePreview instance — a freshly mounted note editor's first pass queues behind the dead one. `passSeq` is keyed on the old (detached) root, so the generation guard never fires for it; only `root.contains(el)` still holds on a detached tree. Frontend unmount path: packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:102-106.

samples.summary: The notes library build now bundles mermaid and emits dynamic chunks: `import('mermaid')` is the package's first dynamic import and the lib build externalizes only @yorkie-js/sdk
samples.evidence: packages/notes/vite.build.ts:19-22 externalizes only `@yorkie-js/sdk`, so every other dependency is inlined into `dist`. `packages/notes/src/view/mermaid.ts:141` (`import('mermaid')`) and `:158` (`import('dompurify')`) are the first dynamic imports in this package (grep for `import(` in packages/notes/src returns only these), so `pnpm --filter @wafflebase/notes build` now inlines mermaid's ~3 MB per-diagram-type graph into the published `dist` and emits extra split chunks alongside the two declared entry filenames, including in the ESM-only-unfriendly `cjs` output declared at package.json `main: dist/wafflebase-notes.cjs`. No in-repo consumer is affected (the frontend aliases the package to source — packages/frontend/vite.config.ts:229), so the impact is on the published artifact only; the frontend chunk-budget bump in the diff does not cover this build.
searchedFor: grep '@wafflebase/notes' across repo for dist consumers
